# Graduate Finance Assistant

 Location: London

 Salary: 30000-35000

 Contract Type: Permanent / Full Time

Graduate Finance Assistant We are really excited to be partnering with a growing business based in Central London on the recruitment of an entry-level Graduate Finance Assistant! You will get stuck into both accounts payable and accounts receivable, which makes this a brilliant chance to get your foot in the door of finance. The manager is genuinely supportive when it comes to growth and development, so you will learn a huge amount and build your experience fast. If you have a degree or are studying towards AAT and want to turn that learning into your first finance role, then this could be the role for you. The business wants someone with real study behind them, plenty of curiosity and a willingness to learn the job from the ground up. You will see how a finance team really works, and be in the Central London office three days a week to learn from the people around you. What You Will Be Doing

- Getting stuck into accounts payable, matching supplier invoices to purchase orders and keeping everything accurate
- Learning how accounts receivable works, from raising sales invoices to posting cash receipts
- Answering supplier and colleague queries by phone and email, and learning when to escalate
- Helping to set up new suppliers and learning why checking bank details properly matters
- Checking staff expense claims and helping to process payments
- Reconciling supplier statements each week, so you really see how the ledgers fit together
- Sending monthly statements to customers and helping chase payments
- Supporting the weekly bank reconciliation and monthly reporting
- Sitting close to your manager, who will teach you the role properly
- Building the skills and confidence to take on more as you grow

 What We Need From You

- Study is a must: a finance or accounting related degree, or AAT studies currently under way
- This is an entry-level role, so a degree or AAT is the right level, rather than ACCA or CIMA
- Prior finance experience would be brilliant but is not essential
- A CV that shows you have gone the extra mile, whether that is internships, volunteering or anything else you have done to gain experience
- Any Excel knowledge, including a course through your studies, which is a real winner
- GCSE Maths and English (or equivalent) and a good eye for detail
- Someone who is happy to settle in and take time to learn, owns their mistakes and asks questions, because in a small team there is nowhere to hide
- Ready to be in the Central London office three days a week, and ideally available at short notice

 What’s in it for you

- A genuine first step into a finance career, with no need for years of experience
- Hands-on training from a manager who is really supportive of your growth and development
- Experience across both accounts payable and accounts receivable from the start
- A small, close team where you will be properly supported and learn faster
- Room to progress as your experience and confidence grow
- Three days in the Central London office, with two working from home

 If this sounds like the perfect place to start your finance career, we would love to hear from you.

The Role: I am recruiting a Trainee Financial Planner / Financial Advisor (Graduate Trainee, Financial Planning Assistant) on behalf of Lifesmiths, a progressive, independent Chartered Financial Planning firm based in Loughton, Essex (IG10).

The Opportunity: the role of Trainee Financial Planner / Financial Advisor (Graduate Trainee, Financial Planning Assistant) provides an exceptional career opportunity for an ambitious individual to establish a rewarding, long-term career in financial planning, working with an interesting portfolio of high net worth clients. You will benefit from a highly structured career pathway, designed to provide outstanding learning opportunities, on-going professional development and the increasing financial rewards that accompany your career progression.

As part of a collaborative, high-performing and client centric team, you will join a business that is genuinely committed to investing in its people. Through ongoing training, mentoring and support, both practically and with professional exams, you will be equipped with the skills and experience required to achieve your full potential, both professionally and financially.

The Career Pathway: You will start your career journey as a Client Support Adviser, where you will complete the first of your professional exams and support with the advice process, learning the basic principles of financial planning and investments. You will then move into the role of Technical Adviser, where you help to shape advice, with involvement in client meetings, drafting suitability reports and producing cashflows. During this stage you will complete additional professional exams, covering tax, trusts and pensions. You will then move into the role of Client Manager, where you will own client relationships, present cashflows and lead sections of the client meetings, working alongside a Chartered Financial Planner. During this stage you will complete your Diploma in Financial Planning (Dip PFS) and continue with the exams required to become Chartered. When your skills and experience allow, you will progress to the role of Associate Financial Planner, where you will manage client relationships end-to-end and be responsible for complex cashflow and financial planning, with some supervision. During this stage you will become Chartered and/or Certified and will reach Competent Adviser Status (CAS). By the final stage, you be a fully qualified Financial Planner and a trusted expert in your profession.

As you successfully progress through each stage, your salary will increase to reflect your growing technical expertise, experience, and level of responsibility.

The Person: The successful Trainee Financial Planner / Financial Advisor (Graduate Trainee, Financial Planning Assistant) will be ambitious, highly intelligent and able to demonstrate a commitment to a career within the financial planning industry. They will be keen to learn, proactive, organised and detail orientated, with exceptional relationship building, customer service and administrative skills. They will be articulate, analytical and aspirational, keen to make a significant contribution to the growth of a forward thinking and ambitious firm while being invested in, valued and rewarded accordingly.

Salary and Benefits: £27,000 to £35,000 (dependant on experience) plus benefits including 34 days’ holiday (23 days annual leave + 3 days Christmas closure + 8 days bank holiday) + 34 hour working week (Monday to Thursday 9am-5pm and Friday 9am-4pm) + 5% employer pension contribution + life insurance + private medical insurance + income protection benefit + ongoing professional training and development. This is an office-based role, so candidates must live (or relocate) within a commuting distance of Loughton, Essex / East London.

The Company: Lifesmiths is a forward thinking, independent Chartered Financial Planning firm who, for over 50 years, has been helping individuals, families and business owners make positive and impactful financial decisions with confidence. A family-owned business with progressive ideas, Lifesmiths combines innovative thinking with strong family values that shape both its culture and the way it supports clients. These values underpin the exceptional levels of service for which the firm is renowned. Committed to helping people create lives of purpose, balance and freedom, Lifesmiths is equally invested in the wellbeing and development of its team. The business has recently embarked on a new chapter, marked by a rebrand and office move, and exciting plans for future growth and development. The Trainee Financial Planner (Graduate Trainee, Financial Planning Assistant) will join a collaborative, supportive and ambitious team, playing an integral role in the firm's continued success while benefiting from excellent opportunities for personal and professional development.

Trainee Financial Planner / Financial Advisor (Graduate Trainee, Financial Planning Assistant), skills and experience required:

- 12 months + experience of working in a professional services environment.
- Highly intelligent, preferably a graduate (ideally 2:1 or above), but this is not essential for an intelligent individual who has chosen to take a different career pathway.
- The ability to demonstrate a commitment to a career with the Financial Planning sector.
- Ambitious, keen to learn and to study for the professional qualifications required to become Diploma qualified and then Chartered/Certified.
- High levels of emotional intelligence, a professional appearance, confident manner and exceptional communication skills, both verbal and written.
- Analytical, excellent administrative and organisational skills and a keen eye for detail
- Strong technology and mathematical aptitude, proficient with MS Office applications.
- A collaborative team player with a “can do” attitude, adaptable to change and prepared to participate fully in the successful operation of the business.

Dawn O’Shea is the Recruitment Partner, recruiting the Trainee Financial Planner/ Financial Advisor (Graduate Trainee, Financial Planning Assistant) directly on behalf of Lifesmiths, so NO AGENCIES PLEASE. If you are successful in being short-listed, you will be contacted by telephone in the first instance to discuss the role and your requirements in more detail

Join our Finance team as an Accounts Payable Administrator and play a key role in maintaining an accurate purchase ledger and supporting the preparation of monthly management accounts and year-end statutory accounts. By processing invoices and payments, reconciling accounts and working closely with suppliers and internal stakeholders, you will help create reliable financial processes that enable our teams to focus on what matters most: better health for more people. Based at our site in Royston with hybrid working available, you will become part of a supportive team of eleven professionals who look forward to shaping the future together with you.

This is an opportunity to grow your purchase ledger experience in a friendly, busy environment at an expanding and innovative company.

Grow With Us – Your Responsibilities

• Take full day-to-day responsibility for the purchase ledger, verify the accuracy of all postings and maintain complete year-end records across eight entities in the UK and Ireland
• Set up and amend vendor records in SAP, including bank-detail changes in line with the Sartorius Fraud Control Policy
• Process planned purchase-order and unplanned non-purchase-order supplier invoices through SAP X-Flow in accordance with the Sartorius authorization and approval structure
• Manage staff expenses and company credit-card expenses through Concur, including finance approvals, employee queries, Corporate and Virtual Credit Card issuance, and payment of external card-provider invoices
• Build and maintain effective supplier relationships, respond promptly to supplier queries by telephone and email, and resolve internal queries in collaboration with Procurement and other departments
• Prepare month-end accounts-payable and supplier-statement reconciliations, manage the GR/IR account, down payments and debit balances, clear intercompany vendor and customer balances where appropriate, and participate actively in monthly balance-sheet reconciliation meetings
• Process daily supplier BACS payments and ad hoc manual or urgent payments, while providing holiday cover for other team members

What Will Convince Us

• You may have A levels in Maths and English
• Previous experience in purchase ledger or accounts
• Previous experience in managing expenses and credit cards
• Intermediate Excel skills; experience with SAP and Concur is desirable
• Strong communication skills and the ability to build effective relationships with internal and external stakeholders
• A highly organised approach, with the ability to take ownership of varied processes, manage priorities and work independently
• A willingness to learn new skills and processes, combined with a collaborative, team-focused approach

In order to commence working with us, the successful candidate must have the right to work in the UK.

What We Offer

As a growing global life science company, stock listed on the German MDAX and TecDAX, Sartorius offers a wide range of benefits:

• Personal and Professional Development: mentoring, leadership programs, LinkedIn Learning, internal seminar offerings
• Making an impact right from the start: Comprehensive onboarding, including a virtual online platform – even before joining
• Welcoming Culture: Mutual support, team-spirit and international collaboration; communities on numerous topics such as coaching, agile working and businesswomen network
• Health & Well-Being: Wide section of health and well-being support such as healthcare plans and health assessment services

Benefits

Attractive Working Conditions:

• 37.5 hours working week
• 25 days annual leave, plus public holidays
• Free parking on site
• Annual option to buy, sell or carry forward annual leave
• Free hot and cold drinks
• Regular social events and free exercise classes
• Competitive benefits package, including:
• Group Personal Pension Plan
• Private Medical Insurance
• Private Dental Insurance
• Group Life Assurance
• Group Income Protection
• Cycle to work scheme

About Sartorius

Sartorius is part of the solution in the fight against cancer, dementia, and many other diseases. Our technologies help translate scientific discoveries into real-world medicine faster, so that new therapeutics can reach patients worldwide.

We look for ambitious team players and creative minds, who want to contribute to this goal and advance their careers in a dynamic global environment.

Join our global team and become part of the solution. We are looking forward to receiving your application.

www.sartorius.com/careers

## Job description

About the role

Location: Bexhill or London

Welcome to Hastings Direct. We're a digital insurance provider with 5 million customers and ambitious plans to become the best and biggest in the UK. Our continued success depends on talented colleagues who are curious, commercially minded and motivated to improve outcomes for our customers. By joining Hastings Direct, you could play a part in the next chapter of our growth and innovation.

Programme overview

Finance is changing, and we want graduates who are ready to help shape what comes next. Over three years, you’ll build a broad understanding of Finance, our business and what drives our performance. Through varied rotations, you’ll gain experience in and learn the fundamentals of different areas of Finance, while working on real business challenges and developing the skills and confidence to contribute from the start. We’ll expect you to be curious, get involved and take ownership. That means delivering the essentials well, but also asking better questions, solving problems, utilising AI and challenging how things are done and looking for opportunities to make a difference. You’ll have the opportunity to explore different areas of Finance and discover where your strengths and ambitions could take you. Perform well and develop at pace, and we’ll look to match you with a permanent role at the end of the programme, based on your interests and the needs of the business.

Pathways

We offer two pathways, with rotations across different areas of Finance designed around your development, interests and experience, alongside the evolving needs of the business.

Finance Forward pathway – Develop into a commercially focused finance professional who helps drive business performance. You’ll use financial and business data to uncover opportunities; challenge thinking and turn insight into action. Along the way, you’ll build data and technology skills, as well as the commercial judgement and influencing skills to make an impact across the business. You’ll also have the option to work towards ACCA, with study support.

Financial Tech pathway – Develop the technology and data skills that will help shape the future of Finance. You’ll use data, automation and emerging technologies to improve how Finance works and drive commercial outcomes, with platforms such as Workday, SQL and Snowflake. You’ll also build a strong understanding of finance and accountancy fundamentals. Your development and qualifications will be tailored to your interests, experience and business needs, helping you build a career at the intersection of finance and technology. Our pathways provide direction, not boundaries. You’ll have the flexibility to gain experience across both and explore opportunities as your interests, skills and ambitions develop.

What you will develop

The programme is intended to build a strong foundation in the fundamentals of Finance, giving you practical experience of the core activities that keep the business running and an understanding of why they matter. Alongside this, you’ll build the capability to solve ambiguous problems with limited guidance, challenge constructively, identify opportunities and risks, and create measurable value through Finance, data, technology and AI. You'll develop the technical, commercial and relationship skills needed to progress towards senior Finance roles. Technology and ways of working in Finance are changing quickly, so continuous learning will be a core part of your career here. You'll be supported to build professional knowledge and if you undertake accounting or technology qualifications, you will be expected to pass relevant examinations in line with company policy.

What we are looking for

- Critical thinking and problem‑solving: You can structure unfamiliar or ambiguous problems, challenge assumptions, evaluate alternatives and reach practical conclusions.
- Clear communication and influence: You can explain complex information clearly, adapt your message for different audiences and contribute constructively to decisions.
- Relationship building, collaboration and emotional intelligence: You work effectively with others, build trust, manage different perspectives and help groups align around a shared objective.
- Curiosity and learning agility: You learn quickly, seek knowledge beyond what is required and apply new skills to real problems. This is particularly important as Finance, data and AI continue to evolve.
- Ownership and initiative: You deliver reliably, take responsibility, look for improvements and act on opportunities rather than waiting to be directed.
- Analytical ability and data literacy: You are confident working with numerical and operational information, identifying root causes, testing assumptions and using evidence to support recommendations.
- Technology and AI aptitude: You are comfortable using digital tools and interested in how automation, data analytics and AI can improve productivity, control and insight.
- Resilience and adaptability: You respond constructively to setbacks, feedback and changing priorities, adapting your approach while maintaining quality and pace.
- Commercial awareness: You are interested in how organisations make money and can connect financial, economic or industry developments to business risks, opportunities and decisions.
- Attention to detail: You follow processes accurately and build in your own checks and controls to maintain high standards.
- Ethical judgement and integrity: You act responsibly, follow appropriate policies and controls, and raise concerns when something does not look right.

No specific degree discipline is required. We welcome candidates from all backgrounds who can demonstrate strong potential, curiosity and an interest in finance, commercial thinking, data and technology.

Timeline

- 23 November 2026 - Applications go live.
- 14 January 2027 11:00 PM - Applications will close.
- 19 January 2027 - Psychometric assessments must be completed by 11:00 PM.
- 25 January 2027 - If successful, you’ll then need to complete a role suitability practical assessment and/or video interview. You’ll receive a new web link for this.
- 8 February 2027 - Deadline for the practical assessment stage.
- 15-19 February 2027 - Successful candidates are contacted and invited to an onsite Assessment Centre.
- 16 & 17 March 2027 - In-person Assessment Centres in Bexhill.

Reward

- Competitive Starting Salary
- Competitive bonus scheme, subject to company and personal performance
- Pension contributions matched up to 10%
- 25 days annual leave
- Access to online learning platforms
- Healthcare cash plan and private medical insurance
- Life cover at 4 x Salary
- Year-round social events, free mortgage advice and more

Right to work and use of AI

Unfortunately, we cannot offer visa sponsorship for our graduate programmes. You must be able to demonstrate your right to work in the UK for the full duration of the programme. We embrace AI as a tool to support our data-driven ambitions and improve how we work. You may use AI tools to help prepare your CV and cover letter. During the assessment process, however, all work must be completed independently and in line with the instructions provided so that we can fairly assess your own knowledge, skills and abilities.

Our 4Cs

Our 4Cs principles are simple. By creating the right culture for our colleagues and giving them the right tools to do their jobs, we deliver good outcomes for every customer, grow the company profitably and sustainably, and invest in the communities we serve. We deliver good outcomes for customers by providing great products at the right price, with a simple and straightforward service. We treat customers as we would want to be treated: fairly, respectfully and with their best interests at heart.

Hastings Group is an equal opportunities employer which means we treat people fairly. We welcome applications from all suitably skilled persons regardless of their gender, age, race, disability, ethnic background, religion/belief, sexual orientation, gender reassignment or marital/family status. Please also note that we have a thorough referencing process, which includes credit and criminal record checks. At Hastings Direct, we’re committed to creating an inclusive environment where everyone has the opportunity to succeed. If you require any reasonable adjustments during the recruitment process, we encourage you to be open with us. Our recruitment team is here to provide the support you need to ensure a fair and accessible experience for all.

Our vision – to be the best and biggest digital insurance provider in the market. It's our attitude and the way we run our business that makes us different. We focus on getting it right for our colleagues, customers, company and community. It's a dynamic, flexible, fun and constantly changing environment. The Vacancy

Join our dynamic TPT Investment Management Team as an intern for 12 months, where you will support our strategic objectives and priorities through research, analysis, and creative contributions. This is an exciting chance to work collaboratively with experienced professionals and develop tools and systems that streamline our investment strategies.

You will be responsible for:

• Collaborating with the rest of the Investment Management Team and supporting key activities.

• Providing input on investment strategies.

• Taking ownership of tasks, proposing ideas, and working creatively under tight deadlines.

• Developing tools & systems for analysing investment strategies and applying policies.

• Analysing economic and performance data to assess whether investment managers are meeting their performance objectives.

• Enhancing and developing reporting tools.

• Analysing large data sets to provide insights to the team.

• Utilising asset-liability modelling software and risk analytics tools.

• Supporting team projects to advance operational priorities and objectives.

• Contributing ideas, challenge practices, and apply academic thought practically.

Skills & qualifications:

• Studying towards a degree with relevance to the areas of responsibility. We will also consider recent (within the last 2-years) Graduates.

• Have a keen interest in and understanding of investment and finance, and how financial history may influence investment decision making and risk management.

• Expert in Microsoft Office Suite, Excel and data analytics.

• Creative thinkers with a methodical and enquiring mind.

• Able to work independently and as part of a team.

What skills will this 12-month internship / placement role develop:

• How to read, analyse and interpret large quantities of data.

• Communication skills, written and verbal.

• Develop your skills in research, data analysis, and project management.

• Stakeholder engagement and team working.

• Report writing and presentation skills.

Why Join Us?

• Gain valuable experience working on real-world projects.

• Collaborate with experienced professionals who will mentor and support you through the start of your career.

• Be part of a diverse and inclusive team that values your unique perspectives.

• Contribute to meaningful change and make a difference in the business landscape.

• Salary £28119 plus benefits

If you are ready to embark on a rewarding internship experience, apply now to become a key player in our Investment Management team in September 2027!

This role will be based up to 4 days in the office in London and 1 day from home.

Please note: this role does not meet the eligibility requirements under the Skilled Worker route and is therefore not eligible for sponsorship

The Company

TPT Retirement Solutions (TPT) is one of the UK’s leading providers of workplace pensions with 80 years’ experience of managing defined benefit and defined contribution pension schemes. It has £11.4 billion of assets under management (as at 30 September 2025) and 490,000 members.

TPT’s mission is to make pension schemes perform better for everyone, from the sponsoring employers and trustees to the members who are saving for the future. They are an innovative, forward-thinking organisation, investing in technology to improve the services they provide. TPT are ultimately owned by a pension fund, providing genuine alignment of interests with those of their clients and scheme members.

Benefits

Competitive salary

Performance-related bonus

Pension scheme

Sports and social events

Training and development plan
